results.execution_guidance: Found 6 tools for this query. Look at the schemas to know how to use them.

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: GitHub is a code hosting platform for version control and collaboration, offering Git-based repository management, issue tracking, and continuous integration features
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=github. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="github") to create a connection BEFORE executing any github tools.

GITHUB_CREATE_A_CHECK_SUITE.description: Creates a new check suite for a specific commit (`head_sha`) in an original repository (not a fork). IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires a GitHub App installation access token - OAuth tokens and classic personal access tokens cannot use this endpoint. GitHub dispatches a `check_suite` webhook event with the `requested` action upon success.

head_sha.description: SHA of the commit for which to create the check suite, typically the head commit of a branch.

GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITO.description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

actor.description: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).

event.description: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

branch.description: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).

status.description: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

created.description: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.

head_sha.description: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).

exclude_pull_requests.description: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.

GITHUB_GET_A_COMMIT.description: Retrieves a specific commit from a repository by its owner, name, and a valid commit reference (SHA, branch, or tag), supporting pagination for large diffs.

ref.description: The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA (e.g., '`sha`'), a branch name (e.g., 'heads/`BRANCH_NAME`' or simply '`BRANCH_NAME`'), or a tag name (e.g., 'tags/`TAG_NAME`'). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.

page.description: Page number for paginating the commit's diff if it's too large. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

owner.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

per_page.description: Number of results per page when paginating the commit's diff (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

GITHUB_LIST_COMMITS.description: Lists commits for a GitHub repository. Requires 'owner' (username/org) and 'repo' (repository name) ...

GITHUB_GET_A_WORKFLOW_RUN.description: Gets a specific workflow run by its ID from a GitHub repository.

GITHUB_LIST_JOBS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN.description: Lists jobs for a specific workflow run in a GitHub repository.
